#1938. Orlando City vs New England Revolution - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 06 Nov 2026 00:13

Orlando City SC host New England Revolution in MLS regular-season action at Inter&Co Stadium on Saturday on Decision Day.

Orlando City SC are guaranteed a seventh consecutive playoff appearance, but they sit ninth in the Eastern Conference table on 43 points, and only a win can lift them level with seventh-placed FC Cincinnati on 46 and, with help from other results, out of the wild-card game.

New England Revolution have a different incentive, as they are third on 58 points, one behind Inter Miami, and a result better than Miami's at home to Charlotte FC would secure the second seed and home advantage through the conference semi-finals.

Orlando City SC won only four of their first 15 league games before the World Cup break, so the club replaced head coach Oscar Pareja with assistant Martin Perelman as interim in March.

The Lions have won eight, lost five and drawn five of their 18 games since the restart, but they are now winless in three, after a 2-2 home draw with New York City FC on October 24 in which they conceded on the last kick.

They then drew 2-2 at Chicago Fire on October 29 after leading 2-0 at half time, and lost 4-0 at Charlotte FC on October 31.

Orlando have conceded 14 goals in their last six league games, and the Charlotte defeat, where Maxime Crepeau saved a penalty only for Abdoulaye Doucoure to score the rebound in the 84th minute, was their first scoreless game in 26 matches across all competitions.

Antoine Griezmann has 14 goals and seven assists in 17 MLS games since arriving in the summer, although his run of 12 straight league games with a goal contribution, which equalled the club record set by Martin Ojeda in 2025, ended at Charlotte.

Perelman can still rely on home form, as Orlando are unbeaten in their last six home league games (five wins, one draw) and have scored 15 goals to six conceded in a run that began on August 22.

New England Revolution have 58 points from 18 wins, 11 defeats and four draws in the first season of head coach Marko Mitrovic, who replaced Caleb Porter after two seasons without a playoff place.

The Revs clinched a playoff berth on October 14 with a 3-2 win at FC Cincinnati and then beat Chicago Fire 1-0, Philadelphia Union 2-1 away and Red Bull New York 3-2 to make it four straight wins.

Daniel Gazdag put the Revolution ahead in the 53rd minute against Inter Miami on November 1, but Lionel Messi scored the winner in the 83rd minute of a 2-1 defeat in front of a season-high 54,112 at Gillette Stadium, which dropped New England from second to third.

Matt Turner made eight saves in the win over Red Bull New York, one short of his career high, and his 18 wins are a Revolution single-season record for a goalkeeper, although the Revs also let a two-goal lead slip to 2-2 by the 64th minute that night.

Dor Turgeman has 12 goals, 10 of them since the World Cup break, while captain Carles Gil has 13 assists this season and reached 100 regular-season assists against Red Bull New York.

Mitrovic has built around young players, with Peyton Miller, who scored twice against Orlando on September 19, starting alongside the 21-year-olds Brooklyn Raines, Ethan Kohler and Joshua Wynder against Miami.

New England Revolution Major League Soccer form:

Orlando were without defenders Griffin Dorsey (back) and captain Robin Jansson (foot) and forward Tyrese Spicer (foot) at Charlotte, and none of them has been confirmed fit to return.

David Brekalo is back after serving a suspension for yellow-card accumulation at Charlotte, but The Mane Land reports that Iago, who was booked there, will serve a suspension in this game.

That leaves Wilder Cartagena, who covered at centre-back for Brekalo at Charlotte, and Brekalo as the likeliest central pairing, with Vinicius Nogueira under pressure at right back after he was substituted at half time following a rough first half.

Griezmann, Martin Ojeda and Ivan Angulo all started at Charlotte with no injury reported, and Angulo's seventh goal of the season at Chicago on October 28 was also his 19th for the club in all competitions.

New England had not published an injury report at the time of writing, but Jack Harrison (quadriceps) and Leonardo Campana continue to be out since March with a lower-body injury.

Alhassan Yusuf (hamstring) has returned from injury and was on the bench against Inter Miami.

Mitrovic started Turner behind Ilay Feingold, Kohler, Wynder and Will Sands against Miami, with Matt Polster and Raines in central midfield and Miller, Gil and Gazdag supporting Turgeman.

Crepeau; Nogueira, Brekalo, Cartagena, Taifi; Angulo, Braian Ojeda, Otavio, Pasalic; Martin Ojeda, Griezmann

New England Revolution possible starting lineup:

Turner; Sands, Wynder, Kohler, Feingold; Polster, Raines; Miller, Gil, Gazdag; Turgeman

New England should edge a high-scoring game because their quick attacks, which produced four goals in the September 19 meeting, face an Orlando defence that has conceded 14 goals in six league games and is short of Jansson, Dorsey and, reportedly, Iago.

Orlando's case rests on five wins in six home league games and on Griezmann, but those results came against sides such as Toronto FC and D.C. United, while their latest games against New England, Chicago and Charlotte brought one point from nine and 10 goals conceded.

Orlando had scored in every match in all competitions since May before the 4-0 defeat at Charlotte, so a goal for Griezmann or Martin Ojeda is more likely than not, which is why we expect the Lions to score twice and still fall one short.

#1937. SBV Excelsior vs Go Ahead Eagles - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 06 Nov 2026 00:22

SBV Excelsior host Go Ahead Eagles at the Van Donge & De Roo Stadion in Rotterdam on Saturday, in round 12 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie.

Excelsior have conceded 19 goals in their last four league games, while Go Ahead Eagles have the Eredivisie's joint-top scorer in Soren Tengstedt but have conceded four times in each of their last two away league matches.

Excelsior collected 10 points from their first five league games to sit fourth in the Eredivisie table after a 2-2 draw at NEC on September 8, and they have taken one point from the 18 available since.

The 0-9 defeat by Twente on November 1 was the heaviest in Excelsior's league history, and it began to unravel when Nesto Groen was sent off after five minutes for a high challenge on Robin Propper, the quickest red card in a league match in the club's history.

Excelsior did not register a single shot and conceded two penalties, and head coach Ruben den Uil said his players had collapsed mentally and stopped carrying out their individual tasks once they fell 2-0 or 3-0 behind.

Excelsior have won one of their five home league games, scoring five goals and conceding 19, nine of them against Twente, while they have taken eight points from six away league matches.

Their 16 league goals include four at Cambuur on August 7, when Noah Naujoks scored twice, so Excelsior have managed 12 in the 10 games since.

That leaves Excelsior 15th on 11 points, two clear of 16th-placed Telstar, who currently hold the relegation play-off place.

Go Ahead Eagles have won three of their 11 league matches without ever winning two in a row, and they sit 10th on 14 points with a goal difference of minus four.

Their latest outing, at promoted Cambuur on October 31, finished 4-0 and was abandoned late in the second half after fireworks were thrown from the away end for a second time, with the KNVB ruling that the scoreline stands.

General director Jan Willem van Dop described the behaviour of the travelling fans as deeply sad, and Go Ahead Eagles are withdrawing away-match registration from supporters identified on footage of the fireworks and the disorder afterwards.

Tengstedt has scored eight league goals, level with Groningen's Brynjolfur Willumsson and Twente's Wout Weghorst at the top of the scoring charts, and he has scored in all five of Go Ahead Eagles' home games, including twice in the 3-2 win over Telstar on October 23.

Head coach Joseph Oosting moved Tengstedt into a free role behind striker Victor Edvardsen against Telstar, with Oskar Sivertsen on the right flank, and the same front four started at Cambuur.

Go Ahead Eagles have conceded in all 11 league games, including four at PEC Zwolle on October 18 and four at Cambuur, the latter with Jasper Cillessen starting in goal for the second time since his debut in the KNVB Beker.

Excelsior are without Groen, who was given a three-match ban with one match suspended, so he misses this game and the trip to Feyenoord on November 21.

Groen scored a stoppage-time winner in the 2-1 victory over Sparta Rotterdam on August 29, and David Garden, who has scored at Cambuur, Willem II and NEC this season, is the likeliest replacement.

Go Ahead Eagles remain without goalkeeper Nick Marsman, who has a knee injury and is not expected back until early January, and defender Pim Saathof, who has not played since May 2025 and is due back around the turn of the year.

Eus Waayers has been sidelined since mid-September.

Stefan Sigurdarson, who has scored against Feyenoord, ADO Den Haag and PEC Zwolle, was among the substitutes at Cambuur and against Telstar.

Cillessen is expected to keep his place in goal ahead of Kjetil Haug after starting the last two matches, and no Go Ahead Eagles player is suspended for the trip to Rotterdam.

Van Gassel; Bos, Widell, Plug, Meissen; Van Vianen, Hartjes, Naujoks; Yegoian, Garden, Sliti

Go Ahead Eagles possible starting lineup:

Cillessen; Sampsted, Dirksen, Kramer, James; Linthorst, Meulensteen; Sivertsen, Tengstedt, Suray; Edvardsen

Go Ahead Eagles have scored 23 league goals to Excelsior's 16 and have the Eredivisie's joint-top scorer in Tengstedt, against an Excelsior back line that has conceded four or more in three of its last four league matches.

The history points the same way, as Go Ahead Eagles have won the last three meetings without conceding, including a 1-0 victory at this ground on March 1, when Tengstedt scored the only goal despite Excelsior having more than half of the possession.

The case for Excelsior is that Go Ahead Eagles are winless in six away league games, have conceded in all 11 league matches, and rely on a scorer who had four goals in his first 41 Eredivisie appearances before this season.

We still expect Go Ahead Eagles to win, because Excelsior have failed to score in three of their last four league matches and are without Groen, so a visiting side that scores twice should be enough even if Excelsior find one goal at home.

#1936. Kaka speaks for the first time since San Siro tears: “Milan is second home to me”

One of the most striking images from AC Milan’s derby win over Inter on Saturday was Ricardo Kaka’s tears as he was welcomed on the field.

Saturday night was the night of Milan’s resounding derby victory – their fourth in a row against Inter – but it was also the night of Kakà’s return to San Siro. He was presented with a trophy before kick-off to mark his induction into the Rossoneri Hall of Fame.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was a moment filled with emotion for all the fans present who chanted his name, but above all it was a moving moment for Kakà himself, who couldn’t hold back the tears as a montage video played on the screen.

Now, the Brazilian has spoken for the first time since that memorable evening as the NSS Sports Instagram page published a short interview with him.

“Milan is a second home to me: that’s the word that comes to mind when I think of this city. I’ve been truly fortunate to have so many great champions at my side, at AC Milan, in the national team, in Madrid: I’ve played with some truly brilliant players.

“The most elegant? Zidane, even though I didn’t play with him, but against him. The best moments associated with San Siro are definitely the victories, the Champions League celebrations in 2007, so many matches like the one against Manchester United or the one against Roma when we won the Scudetto.

“But there were also many moments, every time I entered San Siro and heard the chant ‘Siam venuti fin qua, siam venuti fin qua…’, I got goosebumps.”

#1935. Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

On the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave

Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

New manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1934. Mikel Arteta responds to concerns over ‘exhausted’ Arsenal star after Slavia Prague win

Mikel Arteta has played down concerns over Declan Rice’s fitness after Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

First-half goals from Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres gave Arsenal a commanding lead but Arsenal struggled in the second half and Slavia Prague deservedly pulled a goal back through Wiktor Nowak in the 90th minute.

Rice completed a full 90 minutes in Prague but the 27-year-old showed clear signs of tiredness in the second half.

‘Declan Rice is by far the best midfielder in the country, for me,’ former Arsenal and England Women’s midfielder Karen Carney told TNT Sports after Arsenal’s win.

#1933. Stephen Robinson proud of his battling Dons but injury crisis deepens

Published: 17:30 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 14:43 EDT, 2 November 2026

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson has revealed his injury crisis has become even more catastrophic ahead of the weekend league visit of Hibernian that has the potential to make or break his reign.

The Dons manager saw his side put in a fine, disciplined display in going down 1-0 to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup final, but lost Emmanuel Gyamfi within 15 minutes after he collided with Kim Min-su and also has Brad Lyons battling a knock.

Robinson admitted afterwards that there is no chance of longer-term absentees Chris Cadden, Mats Knoester and Lewis Mayo being available, with Dan Happe the only player likely to return for the Saturday night showdown with Premiership bottom dogs Hibs after being suspended last night.

‘Gyamfi will be out for a long period of time,’ reported Robinson. ‘It looked like it was maybe the other thigh that he’s had a problem with. It’s a heartbreaker for the boy.

‘Brad Lyons took a really bad knock. I’m not sure how serious that is. Hopefully, he’s got away with it.

‘Chris Cadden will be out for six weeks. Mats Knoester is four to six weeks.

Emmanuel Gyamfi limped off early with an injury in Aberdeen's semi-final defeat

‘The only plus point is Dan Happe. It’s very difficult because half the squad are not available. Any team that does well, there’s consistency and patience.

‘Over time, the last person that had prolonged success in Aberdeen was Derek (McInnes). He was given a lot of time and a lot of support, but we’ve not been able to put a consistent team, never mind a consistent shape, on the pitch.

‘It’s four changes every week at the moment.’

Robinson, however, stated his pride in the way his players performed and backed centre-back Jack Milne while taking a pop at the criticism he has come in for of late.

‘They rose against adversity this time. They put in a real performance,’ he said.

‘Rangers scored during our best spell in the game, which is unfortunate, but it’s been a tough week for us with injuries, really tough.

‘They showed great character and courage.

‘Jack’s a young man. Surprisingly, he’s from Aberdeen and he still gets an incredible amount of stick.

‘He’s had one full season and he’s a lovely boy that wants to learn. He’s just learning the game. I thought he showed real character.’

Dons boss Stephen Robinson on the touchline in the 1-0 defeat to Rangers

Robinson also refused to criticise captain Kevin Nisbet after seeing him pass up a couple of golden chances.

‘If you want chances to fall to anyone, it’s Kevin and he had the opportunity to play Mitchy Ntelo in with one of them when clean through,’ he reflected.

‘We had grown into the game. We were organised defensively despite not knowing what our team would be until Saturday morning.

‘I’m proud of the players because they gave me absolutely everything.

‘You’d need to ask the fans if they saw positive performances. I can only answer for myself. I saw a group of boys give everything in adversity.

‘Everyone expected us to roll over and get battered but that wasn’t the case. They’ve shown they have the character to play for Aberdeen in big games, no doubt.’

#1931. Liverpool transfer news: Brazilian heavyweights 'plot audacious swoop' for Anfield star as bitter rivals face the drop

By Seye Omidiora | 06 Nov 2026 00:28

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker has reportedly been identified as a possible target for Brazilian giants Flamengo.

The 34-year-old goalkeeper has recently entered the final 12 months of his current Anfield contract.

Liverpool activated a clause in March to extend his deal by a year, keeping him at the club until June 2027.

However, should the two parties fail to agree another extension, the veteran could leave on a free transfer next summer.

Liverpool face no immediate risk of losing their first-choice goalkeeper, but Flamengo are understood to be assessing whether a bold move is viable.

According to Sport Witness, Alisson's name has been seriously discussed by senior figures involved in Flamengo's long-term plans.

The Rio de Janeiro club are weighing up whether to make a concerted attempt to bring the experienced international back to Brazil.

Some executives feel his proven quality and elite standing would make him a strong addition to the squad.

Others are said to be more sceptical, citing his age and recent underwhelming displays for Brazil.

Flamengo are also facing financial challenges that could significantly limit their spending ahead of next season.

Even without a transfer fee, the club would need to decide whether they could meet Alisson's substantial wage demands.

Should Flamengo choose to pursue their interest, they would face a major geographical and emotional obstacle.

Alisson developed in Internacional’s academy and has previously expressed a wish to return to his boyhood club one day.

Internacional are widely considered his likeliest destination if he eventually moves back to Brazil, but they are currently fighting to avoid relegation.

According to the report, some Flamengo figures are hoping their rivals fall into the second division.

Relegation would weaken Internacional’s ability to persuade Alisson to return or meet his wage demands, potentially putting Flamengo in a stronger negotiating position.

#1929. GdS: Necessities, dreams and surprises – the January mercato Milan have in mind

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is ready to do what is possible to strengthen the squad when the window reopens.

La Gazzetta dello Sport report that the Milan owner is passionate, so while he got emotional after the derby win against Inter, he was also worried following the defeat to Bologna and the limitations it exposed. So, he is ready to give Ruben Amorim a helping hand, but where?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim said that, with the squad reduced by injuries, it’s difficult to press hard and play the football he prefers. We didn’t see that in the derby, but that’s another story.

Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic are the defenders who could use a union representative: they always play, never rest, and almost never come out early. Mario Gila is the other starter, but then Fikayo Tomori and Matteo Gabbia – the natural back-ups – are injured.

That leaves Filippo Terracciano and Sankhoun Diawara, who are more uncertainties than guarantees at present. A signing will arrive and Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio was the target in the summer. The asking price was €40m then, and the Rossoneri could offer it again.

The striker issue is a different story. Milan invested over €70m in Gonçalo Ramos this summer, a deal that is now viewed with some trepidation. It’s right to give Ramos time, but Cardinale has recently fallen head over heels for Nicolò Tresoldi, who scored a hat-trick against Inter in the Champions League.

Tresoldi has been a Milan fan since childhood and doesn’t hide it. Milan would gladly give him the satisfaction of playing for the Rossoneri, but Club Brugge wanted €50m in the summer and it could be more now. Moreover, the De Ketelaere and Jashari negotiations show how difficult they are to deal with.

Will there be any other surprises? A wing-back is possible if Amorim decides the left side needs more momentum, or Samuel Chukwueze finds some company  in the treatment room. A goalkeeper to give Lorenzo Torriani a loan chance is possible. With Cardinale, nothing can be ruled out.

#1928. Mikel Arteta brands Arsenal stars ‘extremely far from our standards’ in Slavia Prague win

Mikel Arteta was not impressed with his Arsenal team in the second half of their 2-1 win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday, saying they were ‘extremely far from our standards’ after the interval.

The Gunners continued their unbeaten start to the Champions League group stage with victory in Czech Republic, with three wins and a draw from their opening four games.

Noni Madueke opened the scoring after just nine minutes and the Premier League champions had a two-goal lead by half-time thanks to Viktor Gyokeres.

Slavia Prague made things difficult for their high profile guests, though, producing 18 shots over the match and scoring a late consolation through Wiktor Novak.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Arteta praised the Czech side, who have picked up just one point from four matches, but accepted that the second half performance from his men left a lot to be desired.

‘First of all, you have to value the fact it’s very difficult to win away from home,’ Arteta told a post-match press conference. ‘We’ve done it against a very tough opponent, we expected that toughness.

‘Two very different halves – the first we played at a really high level in terms of intensity, tempo, quality and clarity in what we had to do, and what the game was demanding. We were very efficient – we should have scored three, four or five.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘We didn’t make that gap, and at half-time, the message was clear. There was still a lot to do in the game – this was a team we were up against with huge spirit, and if you give them something, they will grab it.

‘Right from the beginning of the half, we were extremely far from our standards, the basics, the concepts, and everything we discussed to avoid. It was far from what we expect from each other, but we found a way to hold onto the result and win the game.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The Gunners boss felt his team learned a ‘huge lesson’ in the victory and took responsibility for his players struggling.

‘I already talked about some of the things we didn’t do, and others I’d prefer not to mention,’ he continued. ‘It’s a huge lesson, and we’ll learn from the second half.

‘It’s our third away game in quick succession, and we’re the only team to have played three away games in the Champions League and just one at home – there are a lot of factors – but I don’t like to use that, because in the first half we were at the level we wanted.

‘I take full responsibility for the drop in the second half.’

Goalkeeper David Raya had a similar report to his manager and said Arsenal must improve as the campaign continues.

‘First half, we played really really well. We dominated the whole game, created a lot of chances and could have scored a few more goals,’ he said.

‘We know how important away games are and how difficult places like this can be. They became man-to-man all over the pitch.

‘Delighted with the win, but we’ve got things to improve going forwards.’

#1927. Steve McManaman says he ‘feels sorry’ for two Arsenal stars

Steve McManaman said he ‘felt sorry’ for Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz following Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Slavia Prague as Mikel Arteta’s playing style means the forwards often ‘get the blame’ for the side’s more cautious performances.

Arsenal maintained their unbeaten record in this season’s Champions League as a pair of first-half strikes from Noni Madueke and Gyokeres proved decisive before Wiktor Nowak’s late consolation.

The result ensured the Gunners, last year’s runners-up, sit third four matches into their league-phase campaign following previous victories over Napoli and Lille and a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

September’s 3-0 defeat at the hands of Brighton in the Premier League remains Arsenal’s only loss in all competitions this term, an impressive run that Arteta’s men will look to continue when they return to action at home to Hull this weekend.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Arteta made a total of six changes to his team that got the better of Liverpool on Sunday, with Gyokeres starting through the middle in place of Havertz at Prague’s Fortuna Arena.

The Sweden international has endured a tough start to the new season but played a key role in the opening goal, assisting Madueke with a hooked pass behind Slavia Prague’s defence for Arsenal’s breakthrough inside just nine minutes.

He then got on the scoresheet himself to double the visitors’ advantage shortly before the break, beating Nazar Domchak with a superb effort that went in off the upright.

While it proved a far more difficult second half for Gyokeres as Arsenal held firm to protect their lead, ex-Liverpool and Real Madrid star McManaman felt the striker should have come away proud with his night’s work.

However, the ex-England international expects Havertz to return to Arteta’s starting XI when the north Londoners return to top-flight action against Hull on Saturday.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I liked him in the first half. I think in the second half, when Arsenal became a little bit dishevelled, they weren’t as close to him so I think it’s hard,’ McManaman said of Gyokeres’ performance.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘When they are playing well, he is up there on his own. In the first half, they were very compact, they were very close to him, they were getting around the sides, they were making chances, so he looked dangerous.

‘In the second half, when it got really stretched and they were wide and he was up on his own, he looked as if he was just left alone a lot.

‘I think when Arsenal play as more of a unit, attacking and defending together, I think he looks better.’

Given Arsenal aren’t renowned for being the most ‘entertaining’ of teams, McManaman finds himself ‘feeling sorry’ for Gyokeres and Havertz in certain matches.

‘I do feel sorry for Arsenal forwards sometimes because they’re not an entertaining team, they’re not like a Barcelona. They defend very deep, they defend as a whole and it’s a long way to get to the other end of the pitch to score goals,’ he added.

‘They’re never going to be this entertaining, lovely, free-flowing side scoring goal after goal after goal, and then Gyokeres and Havertz sometimes get the blame because of that. It’s normally the midfielders and the defenders that we talk about.

‘But as I said, Gyokeres had a great first half, he did his best in the second half and he deserves what he got because he got an assist and he got a goal.’

Asked if it could be time for Arteta to trust Gyokeres with more minutes, McManaman replied: ‘Whenever a big game comes around, Arteta reverts to Havertz doesn’t he?

‘People keep saying that Havertz scores goals in the big games and he certainly did that against Liverpool so you can’t really contest that.

‘But I just think he trusts Havertz a little bit more. That’s all it is.

‘Gyokeres played against Slavia Prague and he did exactly what he needed to do. He had an impact on the game, he had a huge impact on the game and we’ll wait and see for Saturday.

‘But I always think that when big games come around, if it was a final or Arsenal or Manchester City, if both Gyokeres and Havertz are fit, then Arteta would always revert back to Havertz.’

Facing the media shortly after the final whistle, Arteta heaped praise on Gyokeres’ all-round display, applauding the Swede’s ‘connection’ with his team-mates.

The Arsenal head coach explained: ‘I thought he was really good. It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use.

‘He’s done it really well, not just for the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s really great news for him, because he really needed that performance.’

On Gyokeres’ combination play, Arteta added: ‘He did that really well, understood really well when to appear, when to threaten, because they leave people, they follow man-to-man in the midfield and leave spaces there.

‘So when I said he was really connected to the team, that was another example. I thought he had a great performance alongside the goal and assist.’

Asked whether not starting had been a challenge for Gyokeres, Arteta replied: ‘It’s a question for him, but I’d imagine every player wants to play every game, and Viktor is no different.

‘The players need to impact the game like he has done today when they get the opportunity, to show the level they can produce. It’s really positive for the team.’

#1926. Lens vs Marseille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 06 Nov 2026 00:42

Fresh off a pulverizing Champions League defeat in midweek, Lens will try to build themselves back up when they welcome Marseille to Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Sunday.

After nine matchdays, Lens sit ninth in Ligue 1, losing 1-0 at Lille last weekend, with OM now two points above them in sixth thanks to a 2-0 win over Toulouse.

Just when Lens seemed to be building some confidence, showing much more consistency domestically, that was all seemingly shattered in midweek.

With a 9-1 Champions League defeat versus Como on Wednesday, Yannick Cahuzac’s men became the first side to concede that many goals in that competition.

After Wednesday’s match, their resilience will be tested like never before, as they hope to avoid losing three successive competitive games for the first time all season.

Their European form has been messy, losing three consecutive Champions League outings by a combined margin of 14-1, though Lens have won three of their last four Ligue 1 affairs.

While they have scored just one Champions League goal at home this season, nine of their 16 domestic goals have occurred at Stade Bollaert-Delelis.

Les Sang et Or have won three of their last four Ligue 1 home meetings against Marseille, coming back to beat them 2-1 in this exact fixture last season.

While Lens are reeling following their midweek fixture, Marseille are feeling much better about their overall form of late.

Bruno Genesio’s men have won four of their last five competitive fixtures, including their first in the Europa League this season at Bayer Leverkusen on Thursday (1-0).

That was their first Europa League away win since 2023 at AEK Athens (2-0), with OM having now won three of their last four competitive games as the visitors.

On Sunday they can collect three successive competitive clean sheets for the first time in 2026, and also pick up consecutive shutouts in Ligue 1 for the first time since March.

Les Olympiens rank second in the league regarding goals per game (2.2) and average possession (55.7%), while only three points currently separate them from second-place Lille.

Marseille have scored seven goals in their last two Ligue 1 away fixtures, two more than they managed in their 10 domestic outings outside Stade Velodrome before that.

Due to adductor pain, Odsonne Edouard is doubtful for Lens, while Ismaelo Ganiou is recovering from knee surgery, Abdallah Sima has a leg issue, Jhoanner Chavez has a sore thigh and Maik Nawrocki is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Ruben Aguilar had their only goal in that embarrassing defeat to Como on Wednesday, while Florian Thauvin has three goal involvements in their last two Ligue 1 affairs at Stade Bollaert-Delelis.

As for Marseille, Derek Cornelius is dealing with a sore hip, Keyliane Abdallah has a knock and Emerson Palmieri is questionable because of a knee issue.

Amine Gouiri has goals in back-to-back competitive outings for OM, netting the winner versus Leverkusen on Thursday, while he and Amine Harit scored in their victory over Toulouse.

Risser; Aguilar, Baidoo, Antonio; Abdulhamid, Bulatovic, Cuisance, Udol; Thauvin, Sotoca; Hazard

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia, Hojbjerg, Nnadi, Abdelli; Mmadi, Gouiri, Paixao

Lens may be shell-shocked when they take to the field on Sunday after that lopsided defeat in Europe this week.

As such, we expect them to play rather timidly, which will play right into Marseille's hands, who are starting to round into form, especially in this competition.

#1925. Bukayo Saka ‘a bit fragile,’ reckons former Arsenal and Manchester United defender

Bukayo Saka is ‘a bit fragile’ and must work on preventing injury problems in future, reckons former Arsenal defender Mikael Silvestre.

The Gunners winger is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem picked up in a Champions League clash with Bayern Munich on October 21.

Saka is not expected to be back in action until December, with Noni Madueke filling in on the right flank in his absence.

The 25-year-old has been hampered by some injury issues over the last two seasons, but has still managed to rack up a huge amount of appearances, 323 for Arsenal in total.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

He played 49 times in all competitions last season, although the 2024/25 campaign saw him play the least since he broke into the first team, turning out 37 times.

Silvestre accepts that injuries are bound to occur for players of Saka’s ilk, but suggests he is not quite as robust as he could be.

‘When you are an explosive player like Saka, obviously the muscles are what will trouble you when you are doing those sprints all the time,’ Silvestre told PariuriX.com. ‘Maybe, he is a bit fragile, and with the amount of games things like this can happen.

‘What is important for him is the recovery and the prevention, because it’s very important for him that it doesn’t happen too often, because he is very important for Arsenal.’

Silvestre sees Madueke as an improving force in Saka’s absence, although there is still room to become sharper in the final third.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘That’s why you have a big squad and Madueke would start for most of the teams in the Premier League, if not all,’ said the Frenchman. ‘He has the quality and I think he is getting his confidence now, he is trying to score and create more.

‘He doesn’t have the killer instinct yet, but he is growing into it and he is trying to get there.’

Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with Manchester United, reckons Arsenal’s forward line as a whole can let them down, with their strength clearly lying in defence. The recent 1-0 win at Liverpool being a good illustration.

‘Winning at Anfield, with a clean sheet as well makes it a very good defensive performance,’ he said. ‘We can’t say the same with the offense. I would say that’s one for the record, and one that you look back at the end of the season and say it was an important 3 points. But it wasn’t a full on, top class, 90 minute performance from Arsenal.

‘But it’s important to get those wins against teams who are also potentially in the race, and to keep your distance from them.

‘The positives are the defensive side of things, the 3 points, and the fact that it was at Anfield. It breaks that negative dynamic but I think it’s just for the stats really.

‘I think you need your best players at the key moments featuring in the semi-finals and the final of competitions. Arsenal need to keep Timber fit, Saliba is coming back also. You need your strong 11 and the best defence once you reach the final. So it’s still a long way away but they defend well, as a unit for sure.’

#1924. Remembrance silence at Arsenal interrupted as North London Forever anthem mistakenly plays ahead of WSL match

Published: 06:38 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 14:53 EDT, 2 November 2026

Arsenal stars and fans were caught by surprise after the club's North London Forever anthem was mistakenly played moments into Remembrance silence before their Women's Super League match with Aston Villa.

Arsenal and Aston Villa had joined the WSL sides paying tribute to the Armed Forces community, past and present, with the fixture having been the Gunners' last women's match at the Emirates before Remembrance Day on November 11.

Players from both sides had gathered by the centre circle, with the stadium announcer then heard requesting fans join in with 'a moment of silence as a mark of respect'.

The silence, however, was unfortunately interrupted when their pre-match anthem The Angel – more commonly known as North London Forever – began playing around the stadium.

Arsenal players, who had bowed their heads for the minute's silence, could be seen quizzically looking at their team-mates as the anthem played.

Players eventually broke away from the centre circle as the anthem continued to play.

Arsenal players lined up for a Remembrance silence, but were visibly surprised when the club's North London Forever anthem played shortly after it began. Source: TikTok - Jodie-woso

Fans commented that they were left confused by the unfortunate interruption to the silence

Shirts from the match, featuring the poppy, are being auctioned in aid of the Royal British Legion

We will remember them. pic.twitter.com/okgfWrEDkQ

The unfortunate moment also caught out fans both in the stadium and watching on television.

'Very disappointed with the apparent mixup with playing north London forever during moment of remembrance, if it was indeed a mistake. All got a bit confusing. Crowd certainly looked confused anyway,' one fan commented.

'Well I’m not convinced North London Forever was supposed to start playing then but okay,' another posted.

'I was watching on tv and I was incredibly confused when NLF started playing, and too make matters worse people were actually singing along,' a third said.

'I was also confused looking around I didn’t know if to sing so I didn’t,' added another.

'As bad as it was, as mentioned it wasn’t going to be a full minutes silence. Also NLF is pre-programmed to play a minute before kick off. Awkward more than anything,' another fan said.

The Gunners shared an image of their players lining up for the tribute on social media, writing 'We will remember them.'

Daily Mail Sport understands Arsenal welcomed members of Islington Veterans Community to Emirates Stadium on Sunday as part of their moment of remembrance.

Arsenal are set to have a full Remembrance commemoration this weekend when their men's team face Hull City on Saturday. The women’s side will also observe a full commemoration at Anfield when they face Liverpool on Sunday.

Arsenal are also among the clubs to have been supporting the Royal British Legion's Poppy Appeal, which has seen poppies woven into their match shirts.

Match shirts are being auctioned on the MatchWornShirt website and app, with net proceeds going directly to the Royal British Legion to support their work with military service members, veterans and their families.

Shirts from Arsenal's WSL fixture against Aston Villa and their Premier League tie at Anfield, which also took place on Sunday, are among the items on auction.

#1923. Le Mans vs Monaco - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 06 Nov 2026 00:47

Le Mans will hope to dig themselves out of the Ligue 1 relegation zone Sunday when they host Monaco at Stade Marie-Mavingt.

A 2-0 defeat at Troyes last week dropped MUC72 down to 17th in the table, while Monaco sit seventh after a 3-1 loss at Paris FC.

The wheels appear to have fallen off Le Mans since the season resumed after the fall international break.

Before the October window, Patrick Videira’s men had earned points in four of their first five league contests, but they will enter this weekend on a four-match winless run in this competition.

They have just one point domestically since October, which is part of the reason they sit in the final relegation spot heading into this game.

Despite their recent poor form, they are only a point below Angers and Ligue 1 safety heading into matchday 10, with only three points currently separating them from Toulouse, who are 12th.

This team have been at their best domestically at home this season, earning points in three of those four outings, scoring six of their 11 goals at Stade Marie-Mavingt.

Les Mucistes will try to avoid suffering consecutive defeats at home in the French top flight this weekend for the first time since March 2010.

The Monaco team that we saw begin this season so well have been a shadow of themselves in recent weeks domestically.

Filipe Luis has seen his side drop points in four successive Ligue 1 affairs, with the Brazilian particularly annoyed with their performance against Paris FC.

His team bounced back in midweek, defeating Nordsjaelland in the Conference League (2-0) to maintain their 100% record in that competition.

Their triumph on Thursday made Luis just the fifth Ligue 1 manager to win his first five European matches in charge of a French club and only the second this century after Peter Bosz did so at Lyon in 2021.

On Sunday, Monaco can end a two-match losing run away from home in Ligue 1, netting just once over that stretch.

Les Monegasques can stretch their competitive unbeaten run versus Le Mans to nine matches this weekend, having come away with points in their last four away games against them.

Former Monaco defender Djibril Sidibe could miss another match for Le Mans this weekend due to a foot injury, while Erwan Colas remains questionable because of a knock.

Adil Bourabaa will not be available as the central midfielder is still recovering from ankle surgery with his return likely to be sometime in early 2027.

At Monaco, Stanis Idumbo has a knock and could miss this game, and Ansu Fati remains questionable with a sore hamstring.

Folarin Balogun netted his first of the season in their loss to Paris FC, with Mathys Detourbet and Matthis Abline scoring in their Conference League triumph on Thursday, the first for the Manchester City loanee with the Principality club.

#1919. The Man Utd change Michael Carrick must make against Aston Villa to keep his job

With JJ Gabriel almost out the door at Old Trafford Manchester United, and Michael Carrick will now be tempted to pin all their hopes on another emerging star in Shea Lacey.

The 19-year-old has played himself into first-team contention after a dazzling display off the bench in Tuesday’s comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League.

While it was Bruno Fernandes’ penalty that sparked the revival and Matheus Cunha’s brace that got them over the line, Lacey’s fearless cameo on the right was the catalyst for change.

Even the perennially reserved Michael Carrick couldn’t hide his delight over the performance, noting the teenager has ‘that bit of mischief’ in his locker that troubled Roma for the final 15 minutes of the game. Lacey ended the contest playing in defence after Cunha’s red card with Carrick jokingly christening him his new right-back.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Lacey’s sharp, perfectly-weighted passing enabled United to get up the pitch with real intent – seldom seen this season. He completed every one of his attempted passes and completed all but one of his duels. Operating in tight spaces just in front of the touchline, his first touches and clever exchanges were on point from the moment he came on. His pass for Cunha’s winner couldn’t have been placed better.

It has been a long time coming for Lacey. Injuries shelved tentative plans for him to make his debut at 16 under Erik ten Hag in 2023 and it was a tough road back from those issues that threatened to halt his progress.

‘Everybody in the world knows about Shea Lacey,’ United’s former Under-21 manager Travis Binnion said last year. ‘So he needs a little bit of fortune, he needs to be patient with himself and everybody else needs to be really patient with him.’ That patience could now be about to pay off.

Whether Tuesday’s win was a turning point or another false dawn for United remains to be seen. Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer led United to delirium-inducing comeback victories over Newcastle United in Atalanta with identical scorelines when the pressure was mounting on their shoulders. Both were gone shortly after.

But with Carrick’s back against the wall, there is the opportunity to roll the dice with Lacey. The Liverpool-born talent thumped home a wonderful strike in the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton but has seen just 31 minutes of action off the bench since. Excluding the second-half performance against Roma, United’s attack has lacked any verve or real invention. A change is needed and Lacey will feel this is his chance.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It was on the right where he caused damage midweek with Amad Diallo making way for him after 75 minutes. It had been another disappointing evening for the Ivory Coast international who spurned huge opportunities against Chelsea four days earlier.

Since forcing his way back into the side under Erik ten Hag, Amad has been looked upon as United’s most naturally talented winger. But his goal and assist return has fallen woefully short of expectations. He is now approaching one year without a goal, last finding the back of the net in the 4-4 draw with Bournemouth on 15 December. In that time, he has provided two assists – one on the final day of last season against Brighton and the other for Joshua Zirkzee’s consolation goal in the 4-1 humiliation in Como two weeks ago.

His haul of 14 goals during his magnificent campaign with Sunderland in the 2022-23 season is a distant memory. A hat-trick against Southampton in January 2025 helped him to an impressive haul of 11 goals and 10 assists in his first full campaign back in Manchester but seven goal involvements in 40 appearances since the start of the 2025-26 campaign is not good enough.

Wayne Rooney alluded to Amad’s problem midweek and made his case for Lacey getting the nod.

‘Amad does some really good things, but it’s that end product, that is what takes you to the next level,’ he told Amazon Prime. ‘And the glimpses of what I’ve seen from Lacey when he has come on…he has got something in there, that little touch and little pass which United needed to get them over the line in this game.’

The win over Roma has shifted a few clouds amid the gloom hanging over Old Trafford and Sunday’s visit of Aston Villa now looks a more inviting environment for Carrick to make the change and put his faith in Lacey.

#1918. Ex-Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United star Sebastien Bassong is fined for dodging £7 Tube fare by using someone else's travelcard

Published: 13:02 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 16:13 EDT, 2 November 2026

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Sebastien Bassong has been fined for dodging a £7 Tube fare after he was caught using someone else's train driver pass illegally.

The Frenchman, 40, who spent several seasons in the Premier League with Spurs, Newcastle and Norwich, was stopped by a Transport for London (TfL) officer after he was spotted tailgating a friend through the barriers at St Paul's station in May.

The ex-footballer was carrying the Oystercard of the friend's ex-girlfriend, which had been issued to her as a driver on the Docklands Light Railway (DLR), court documents showed.

The TfL officer was then told that Bassong, who was an £8 million signing for Spurs in 2009, had been using her travelcard because he was 'experiencing financial and personal hardship due to a divorce and unemployment'.

Bassong was convicted of using the rail network without a valid ticket at Wimbledon Magistrates Court on October 30.

Magistrate Graham Burbage fined him £220, ordered him to pay the £7 fare for his journey from Arnos Grove to St Paul's, and directed him to pay £250 in prosecution costs and an £88 victim surcharge.

Bassong did not enter a plea to the charge, and was convicted behind closed doors in a Single Justice Procedure hearing.

Adebukola Anifowose, a revenue control officer for TfL, told the court in a statement she spotted Bassong at 1.08pm 'pretend to tap an Oystercard enclosed in a white wallet before tailgating through the wide-aisle gate behind another male'.

Sebastien Bassong in action during a Premier League match between Chelsea and Tottenham at Stamford Bridge in 2009

Bassong attended the 2026 PFA Awards at the Manchester Opera House

The star playing for Spurs during the UEFA Champions League  match between BSC Young Boys and Tottenham Hotspur in 2010

She said Bassong offered up a TfL staff nominee pass when challenged, which allows free travel on London transport.

'System checks later confirmed that the pass did not belong to him and had last been used in October 2025,' she said.

'The accompanying male was spoken to – this individual later informed me that he was assisting Mr Bassong, who was experiencing financial and personal hardship due to a divorce and unemployment, by providing him with the nominee pass.

'It was subsequently established that the pass was registered to an ex-girlfriend of this male, who reportedly claimed to be a DLR driver.'

A notice about the prosecution was sent to Bassong's north London home, and he did not respond before the court hearing.

Bassong, who now runs a motivational coaching business, has been given 28 days to settle the court bill totalling £565.

#1915. Austin FC vs Portland Timbers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 06 Nov 2026 01:09, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 08:59

Austin FC host Portland Timbers in a Major League Soccer Decision Day fixture at Q2 Stadium on Saturday.

A win would clinch a playoff place for Portland, while Austin, already eliminated, play the last match of Davy Arnaud’s interim spell before Jim Curtin takes over.

Austin FC sit 14th in the Western Conference and were eliminated from playoff contention by consecutive defeats to Real Salt Lake on October 28 and LA Galaxy on October 31.

Arnaud has been in charge on an interim basis since Nico Estevez was dismissed on May 18, and Curtin, the former Philadelphia Union head coach, takes over on December 1 or at the end of the season, whichever is later.

The Galaxy defeat was settled early, with Joao Klauss scoring in the 10th minute, Hirving Lozano in the 38th and Robert Taylor in the 48th to leave Austin three goals down before the hour.

Ervin Torres pulled one back in the 54th minute with a long-range strike for his second career MLS goal, set up by Micah Burton - who was making his first MLS start - and Jorge Alastuey, before Sergi Roberto made it 4-1 in the 66th minute.

Damian Las made two saves in the 35th minute to keep the score at 2-0 at that stage, and Riley Thomas came off the bench to make his MLS debut.

On a brighter note, Austin have scored in each of their last seven matches, having last been held scoreless by FC Dallas on September 20.

Myrto Uzuni and Christian Ramirez both have nine goals and would reach double figures with a goal on Saturday.

Austin also won the last meeting 2-1 at Providence Park on August 29, with Facundo Torres scoring the opener and Oleksandr Svatok netting the winner in stoppage time.

Portland Timbers are eighth in the West on 43 points, with 12 wins, seven draws and 14 defeats from their 33 matches, and a run of three straight victories has lifted them into a wild-card position.

Marti Cifuentes’s side were in a seven-game winless run between early September and mid-October, so a third successive playoff appearance in his first season would mark a sharp turnaround.

The three wins came against Charlotte FC, St. Louis City and Houston Dynamo, all of whom are heading to the post-season, and the Timbers scored nine goals across those fixtures.

The 3-1 victory over Houston on November 1 featured a 18-8 shot advantage, with six efforts on target compared with one for the visitors.

Vincent Janssen, a mid-season signing, scored his fifth goal of the season against Houston and added two assists, the first of his MLS career.

Kristoffer Velde scored his 11th goal of the season in the same game, and American Soccer Analysis rated him the most valuable outfield player in MLS outside Lionel Messi since the World Cup break.

David Da Costa scored the opener and took his team-leading assist tally to 11 from the corner that Janssen headed in for the third.

The Timbers rank ninth in MLS for goals scored but 22nd for goals conceded, and they have kept only two clean sheets this season.

A win clinches a playoff place and keeps seventh spot and a round-one berth, within reach, while a draw only secures qualification with help from other results.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:

Austin will do without Chris Applewhite (quad) and Jon Bell (lower abdomen) for Matchday 34, while Zan Kolmanic is suspended following his red card against LA Galaxy.

Uzuni and Ramirez are both available to chase double figures, and Facundo Torres, scorer of the August opener in Portland, is also available.

Portland have six players listed as out: Alex Bonetig (shoulder), Brandon Bye (knee), Jimer Fory (concussion), Zac McGraw (back), Juan Mosquera (foot/ankle) and goalkeeper Trey Muse (concussion).

Janssen, Velde, Da Costa and Ariel Lassiter are all available again.

Las; Desler, Sanchez, Biro; Burton, Sabovic, E. Torres, Alastuey; Placheta, Gallagher, Ramirez

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:

Pantemis; Hernandez, Surman, Waterman, Smith; Izoita, Caicedo, Da Costa; Lassiter, Velde, Janssen

Portland arrive with the clearer motivation and the stronger recent evidence, as nine goals in three wins against playoff-bound opponents sit alongside a front line in which Janssen, Velde and Da Costa are all producing.

Austin conceded three goals inside 48 minutes at the Galaxy, are heading for a bottom-two finish in the West, and have nothing to play for beyond individual milestones and the chance to give their academy players further minutes.

The Timbers have not lost in Austin since 2021, and their need for a result should decide a game in which both sides score.

United prepare to face Villa sitting just 17th in the Premier League, two points above bottom-placed Sunderland, and having won only one of their opening nine games.

Aston Villa, in contrast, are unbeaten in five league games following a slow start to the campaign, with their recent upturn in form taking them into the top-half of the table.

Unai Emery’s side have lost two of their last three games, however, suffering a Carabao Cup exit at the hands of Bournemouth before losing to Barcelona in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

But Carragher expects Aston Villa to return to winning ways at Old Trafford, and inflict a potentially fatal blow on under-fire Manchester United boss Carrick, predicting a 2-1 away victory.

Looking at some of this weekend’s other Premier League fixtures, Carragher told Sky Sports: ‘This weekend’s line-up is looking cracking.

‘Arsenal should get over the line comfortably against Hull, after taking the top spot last week. Same goes for Manchester City, they should get back to winning ways against Nottingham Forest.

‘Elsewhere I’m confident Liverpool will pick up all three points against Crystal Palace.’

The Red Devils beat Aston Villa 3-1 in this fixture back in March after losing 2-1 at Villa Park earlier in the campaign.

Ironically, Emery has been heavily linked with Manchester United amid growing pressure on ex-England midfielder Carrick.

But reports say the Spaniard is set to sign a new contract to extend his spell at Villa Park after last season’s Europa League triumph.

While Emery will not be taking over at Old Trafford any time soon, Manchester United have shown interest in Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte.
